correctness.rationale: I enumerated every six-edge subset of the eighteen graph edges and accepted exactly those covering all twelve vertices, giving 20 perfect matchings and 822 augmented faces. An independent unit-pivot order split off 408 contractible integral pairs, leaving six free degree-two generators and zero differential. For each group element I generated the complex of its edge-orbits whose unions lie inside perfect matchings. A setwise-fixed simplex of k edges formed from j orbits has permutation sign (−1)^(k−j), so its signed Lefschetz contribution is (−1)^(j−1); the empty face contributes −1. The four orbit-complex reduced Euler rows were (6,0,0,0,0,0), (2,2,2,−4,2,2), and two copies of (0,−2,0,−2,0,−2), reproducing all 24 traces without using the supplied fixed-face parity calculation. The rational planes can each be realized on Q(ζ₆), with multiplication by ζ₆^j and conjugation as the generators; their characters and those of the lines give exactly the proposed decomposition. Semisimplicity and equality of characters in characteristic zero identify the rational module. Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/audit-2.py.
residual_risks: No assertion about the integral group-ring module follows from this computation. The frozen ancillary self-review's mention of a four-sphere is not adopted: for n=6 all six spheres of Theorem 25 are two-dimensional, consistent with RESULT.md.

value.rationale: The perfect-matching complex and its full geometric symmetry action are natural before choosing a computation. Six rungs are the meaningful boundary where the two homological contributions of the circular-ladder theorem merge in one degree. The result identifies both layer orientations of the frequency planes and the reflection-sensitive lines, information needed to analyze invariant subspaces or compare symmetry-respecting reductions. It is not just the known rank or a single numerical trace.
residual_risks: No equivariant homotopy type or result for arbitrary other widths is certified.
